basic.d: Two tiles already known to be in different pieces have a wall between them.

size.d: Two groups that are too big together get a wall between them.

grow.d: A group that is still too small grows through its only way out.

min-grow.d: A group below the Minimum grows through its only way out.

reach.d: A group joins the tiles it needs to reach an allowed size.

min-reach.d: A group joins the tiles it needs to reach the Minimum.

rose-grow.d: A group that still misses a rose type grows through its only way out.

rose-reach.d: A group goes the only way that leads to a rose it still misses.

rose-pair.d: Two roses of the same type are in different pieces.

rose-cut.d: When roses are behind a narrow passage, each passage tile leads one piece to its roses.

stamp-place.d: Edges outside every place the stamp's shape fits are walls, edges inside all of them are open.

stamp-size.d: A stamp's piece is never bigger than its shape.

stamp-shape.d: A stamp's piece never leaves its shape.

stamp-pair.d: Two stamps of the same shape that one shape cannot cover are in different pieces.

shape-fit.d: A group has to stay inside the stamp's shape.

bank-fit.d: A group has to stay inside one of the bank shapes.

ban-fit.d: A group never becomes a shape of the Omits.

bank-place.d: Edges outside every place a bank shape fits are walls, edges inside all of them are open.

bank-region.d: A closed-in area can be cut into bank shapes in only one way.

bridge-count.d: At a single connection between two sides, only one choice leaves each side a number of tiles that whole pieces can cover.

area-sum.d: When the area numbers add up to every tile, each tile joins a numbered piece.

area-region.d: The area numbers of a closed-in area fit in it in only one way.

area-place.d: Every place the numbered piece can take agrees on this edge.

area-rel.d: A wall that compares sizes leaves only some sizes for the pieces on its two sides.

range-count.d: Only some sizes can still fill the whole board, and these two groups together would have none of them.

range-region.d: A closed-in area is cut into whole pieces of the allowed sizes in only one way.

euler-count.d: When only a few pieces are allowed, there are only so many walls.

colour-count.d: When only a few pieces are allowed, groups that cannot be different pieces are the same piece.

match-place.d: With Match, edges outside every place the one shape fits are walls, edges inside all of them are open.

match-region.d: With Match, a closed-in area with the size of one piece is one piece.

match-fit.d: With Match, one shape has to fit every group.

match-size.d: With Match, only some sizes can fill the whole board.

match-mismatch.d: Match and Mismatch together leave one single piece.

mismatch-place.d: With Mismatch, a group that can only become one shape follows the places that shape fits.

mismatch-link.d: With Mismatch, two groups that can only become the same shape are one piece.

mismatch-hall.d: With Mismatch, pieces that can only be a few shapes take them all, and the others lose those shapes.

mismatch-count.d: With Mismatch, each size has only so many shapes, so only some sizes can fill the board.

mingle-area-link.d: With Size Separation, two neighbours that must have the same size are one piece.

mingle-shape-link.d: With Mingle Shape, two neighbours that must have the same shape are one piece.

mingle-area-merge.d: With Size Separation, groups that end with different sizes are different pieces.

mingle-shape-merge.d: With Mingle Shape, groups that end with different shapes are different pieces.

mingle-area-parity.d: With Size Separation and only two sizes, the sizes alternate across every wall.

mingle-shape-parity.d: With Mingle Shape and only two shapes, the shapes alternate across every wall.

mingle-area-place.d: With Size Separation, a piece of known size only goes where it touches no piece of that size.

mingle-area-single.d: With Size Separation and only one size possible, no two pieces can touch: the board is one piece.

mingle-shape-single.d: With Mingle Shape and only one shape possible, no two pieces can touch: the board is one piece.

solitude-grow.d: With Solitude, a group without a symbol grows through its only way out.

solitude-reach.d: With Solitude, a group goes the only way that leads to a symbol.

boxy-place.d: With Boxy, edges outside every rectangle that fits are walls, edges inside all of them are open.

boxy-line.d: With Boxy, a piece with a prime number of tiles is a straight strip.

boxy-corner.d: With Boxy, walls never bend at a corner.

boxy-fill.d: With Boxy, a piece fills the smallest rectangle around its tiles.

nonbox-grow.d: With Non-boxy, a group that is still a rectangle grows through its only way out.

pal-wall.d: A palisade gets exactly its number of walls: this side has to be one.

pal-link.d: A palisade gets exactly its number of walls: this side has to stay open.

pal-pair.d: Two palisades side by side share a side, which counts for both.

pal-two.d: When only two pieces can exist, every wall has the same two pieces on its sides.

pal-size.d: A palisade's open sides give its piece a smallest size.

wally-wall.d: With Wally, a tile never has three neighbours in its piece.

wally-link.d: With Wally, a tile keeps at most two neighbours in its piece, and here only one way is left.

wally-ends.d: With Wally, a piece is a path with two ends.

gemini-place.d: Across a Gemini wall both sides keep the shapes they share; across a Delta wall they cannot end the same.

bri-three.d: With Bricky, four walls never meet at a corner: after three, the fourth edge is open.

bri-pinch.d: With Bricky, two tiles of one piece that touch at a corner are joined through a third tile.

loo-outline.d: With Loopy, no wall touches the outline.

loo-three.d: With Loopy, an even number of walls meets at every corner: after three, the fourth edge is a wall.

loo-corner.d: With Loopy, at a corner where a hole pokes in, the two other edges are both walls or both open.

loo-color.d: With Loopy, a wall changes the colour of a tile and an open edge keeps it.

tower-wall.d: A watchtower counts the pieces around its corner: here the tiles have to be apart.

tower-link.d: A watchtower counts the pieces around its corner: here the tiles have to be together.

tower-wrap.d: A piece never wraps around a watchtower corner.

compass.d: A compass piece goes the only way that gives it enough tiles on that side.

cmp-block.d: A tile out of the compass piece's reach is cut off by a wall.

cmp-budget.d: A compass number is exact, so the piece has only so many tiles to spend on its way to a rose.

cmp-wrap.d: The compass piece needs this tile to have enough tiles on one side.

cmp-place.d: Tiles in every piece that fits the compass are joined, tiles in none of them are cut off.

cmp-crowd.d: Several compasses share the tiles, and only one choice leaves enough for each.

cmp-excl.d: A tile that breaks the compass numbers stays out of the piece.

cmp-box.d: With Boxy, a compass counts whole rows or columns of its rectangle.

diff-clash.d: A piece with two Difference walls of different numbers has two different neighbours.

diff-small.d: With Mismatch and a Maximum, Difference walls need small pieces, and there are only a few.

label.d: Every tile belongs to the piece of one clue, and here only one clue is left for it.

box-hall.d: With Boxy and Mismatch, pieces that can only be a few rectangles take them all.

region-merge.d: In a closed-in area, the sizes the walls ask for fit only with these groups as one piece.

size-cut.d: When every piece has the same size, the tiles behind one narrow tile have to make whole pieces.

hetero-link.d: With Heterogeneous, two neighbours that must have the same size are one piece.

hetero-merge.d: With Heterogeneous, groups that end with different sizes are different pieces.

hetero-parity.d: With Heterogeneous and only two sizes, the sizes alternate across every wall.

hetero-place.d: With Heterogeneous, a piece of known size only goes where it touches no piece of that size.

hetero-single.d: With Heterogeneous and only one size possible, no two pieces can touch: the board is one piece.

fact:far-join.d: Tiles that are far apart can be known to be in one piece before the way between them is known.

fact:label-join.d: Tiles that can only belong to the same clue are one piece, even far apart.

fact:clue-join.d: Two clues that cannot be in different pieces are in one piece.

fact:pair-join.d: Two groups that cannot be different pieces are one piece.

fact:split-cut.d: When only one way connects two tiles of a piece, that way is part of the piece.
